cuts.reason: Cuts from the wide establishing shot of the husband's 'low battery' body drooping at the stove to a tight reaction shot on the wife, right as she begins her line about how long he's been running down -- setting up the joke's premise on her face.

Cuts back to a close-up on the husband's head atop his slumped, powered-down body just after the wife finishes her punchline ('...minutes'), landing on his reaction as the visual payoff of the low-battery gag.
Hard cut to the black title card ('Low Battery People, created by Nin.') immediately after the husband's beat, ending the sketch right on the joke without a fade or lingering resolution.

reaction_shots.description: Sustained close-up on the wife's droopy, unimpressed face as she delivers the setup/punchline dialogue, with the husband's collapsed 'low battery' body soft-focus in the background -- her deadpan expression carries the comedic tone.
Close-up on the husband's head perched atop his slack, powered-down felt body, blinking in a dopey low-battery reaction that pays off the wife's line.

pacing_notes: The scene opens with the longest shot (~4.8s) to establish the setting and the sight gag of the husband's melted, low-battery posture, then holds even longer (~6.8s) on the wife's static reaction shot to let the punchline dialogue land in a single unbroken take. The pace then quickens with a short (~2.8s) reaction cutaway to the husband's face for the visual payoff, before an abrupt hard cut to a brief (~1.4s) title card ends the video immediately after the joke, with no dissolve or coda.
